title: RBI Hikes Repo Rate to 5.50% in First Increase in Nearly Four Years
excerpt: The six-member MPC voted unanimously to raise rates and shifted its stance to "calibrated tightening" as inflation climbs to 4.8%.
body:
• The RBI's six-member MPC unanimously raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% on October 7, 2026 — its first hike in nearly four years.
  • The policy stance shifted from neutral to "calibrated tightening", signaling the easing cycle is over and further hikes are possible.
  • The RBI raised its FY27 GDP growth forecast to 7.1% while lifting the inflation projection to 5.2%, citing food, fuel and global crude pressures.

The Reserve Bank of India's Monetary Policy Committee has raised the benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%, ending a nearly four-year pause and launching a new tightening cycle as inflation pressures build. All six MPC members voted unanimously for the hike at the committee's 63rd meeting, held October 5–7 under Governor Sanjay Malhotra.

https://x.com/RBI/status/2107705633873309910

The move was widely anticipated — a Reuters poll of 61 economists had 35 expecting exactly this outcome — but the simultaneous shift in stance from "neutral" to "calibrated tightening" gave the decision a hawkish edge. The new stance effectively rules out rate cuts and leaves the door open for further tightening depending on how inflation and global conditions evolve.

Driving the decision: headline CPI inflation climbed to 4.8% in August from 4.5% in July, with price pressures spreading from food and fuel into core inflation. The RBI now expects FY27 inflation at 5.2%, peaking near 6% in the third quarter. At the same time, the economy is running hot — Q1 FY27 GDP grew 7.8%, and the central bank raised its full-year growth forecast to 7.1% from 6.7%, giving it room to act against inflation without fearing a growth shock.

Other policy rates moved in step: the standing deposit facility rate rose to 5.25%, while the marginal standing facility rate and bank rate climbed to 5.75%. The cash reserve ratio was left unchanged at 3%.

Markets took the hawkish signal in stride but repriced accordingly. The Sensex fell 574 points and the Nifty slipped 0.94% on the day, while the 10-year government bond yield hardened 5–6 basis points to around 7.25%. Economists noted the hike was fully priced in; the stance change, however, surprised some, with at least one major AMC now expecting another 25bp hike at the December policy meeting.

For the diaspora, the decision cuts both ways. A firmer rate differential should lend the rupee some support against a strong dollar and steady portfolio flows — good news for anyone watching the exchange rate on remittances. But borrowing costs will edge higher for rate-sensitive sectors: NRIs with home loans in India or exposure to housing, autos and NBFCs should expect EMIs to tick up, while returns on NRI deposits and FCNR accounts are likely to improve as banks pass through higher rates.
